title: Agent architectural review and ground-up rebuild

completion_criteria.text: Current-state audit complete: every gap in the roster, the agent definitions and the observation machinery identified with measured evidence from the ledger and the definition files.
Audit delivered in a form the user can read and navigate - a self-contained HTML explainer with diagrams, written for a reader with no prior domain knowledge.
Target architecture designed and approved by the user: roster shape, tool grants, who may delegate, and how the configuration observes itself.
Agent and observer teardown and rebuild executed without breaking the live coupling surface: rules and skills naming agents by string, 405 worktree copies, four backup profiles, derived residuals.
New configuration verified in real use: dispatch routes to the intended agents, and the observation system attributes every run and records an outcome.

spine.active_goal: Get the target architecture to explicit user approval so c3 can close, then execute the teardown and rebuild at c4.
spine.next_step: WAIT for the user's SPECIFIC instructions. Do NOT auto-proceed, and do NOT edit any agent, rule, hook or skill file. The round-4 report at ~/.agent/diagrams/agent-roster-rebuild-recommendations.html is amended, gate-clean and awaits the user's MANUAL REVIEW. Read section 2e first: this round reversed the report's own strongest measurement. Every round-4 recommendation is awaiting-ruling; records 0487, 0490 and 0491 are settled, and 0493 is now shipped and verified live on main.
spine.last_session: PR 153 merged to main (b306a44f) and confirmed IN FORCE, not just merged: the live analyzer is byte-identical to origin/main, local main fast-forwarded off the pre-fix blob, and the branch deleted locally and on origin with all three refs verified gone. No agent, rule, hook or skill file edited.

open_risks.text: Never read `emitter` in the events log as a measurement — it is a hardcoded constant on every row, and treating it as signal already produced one wrong conclusion
Archive the events log before any teardown step — 8.7 MB across 46 days is the only artifact here that cannot be regenerated, and it is the baseline a new roster gets measured against
Repoint the five skills that name deleted agents — verification-discipline and report break outright, since every branch of their logic invokes verification-strategist and report-writer by name
Land the new mitosis engine before starting the rebuild — this work targets that engine, whose dispatch table comes from engine source literals rather than a static allowlist

Run the preserved validator before AND after every edit to the report — its ratified baseline is exactly two failing checks, so a third failing check means that session introduced a regression rather than hitting a known one
refs: same directory: run-fixture-suite.mjs, README.md, round4-findings.md, round4-addendum.md, decision 0491 defines the ratified baseline

open_risks.text: Sharpen report section 11a from the observer reads the wrong file to the observer was verified by a probe that could not fail — that is the transferable lesson for the rebuild, and it is a live instance of the report's own risk R5

Fix the false destructive-operation confirmation claim in all four files before any volume work on the instruction layer — the gate's ask verdict was removed from source, so the claim is false, and a correctness defect outranks a token cost

Add StructuredOutput to each agent's explicit tools list rather than deleting the lists — all 15 current agents declare explicit allowlists, and although an absent tools line inherits the full tool set, deleting a list would widen permissions far past the fix
Delete the two confirmed dead agent references before they mislead a future reader — both name agents that exist nowhere on disk or in any installed plugin

Choose which browser tooling is standard for reproducing a user-interface bug — what a reproduction must RETURN is now settled as a re-runnable command plus inputs rather than a screenshot, so only the tool choice remains open
Decide whether this thread supersedes the paused thread agent-roster-gap-resolution — it covers overlapping ground against an older SPEC and was not touched in rounds 2, 3 or 4

key_decisions.title: The audit pass characterises the current state and recommends nothing
Replace all 56 agents with 13 in four bands, with the dispatch tool held only by the Opus leads
Terminate review loops by closing the reviewer's question, not by capping rounds or turns
Rebuild the observer to append one line per run and do everything else at audit time
Put load-bearing rules in agent bodies, generated from shared fragments with a drift check
User rulings on the six open rebuild questions, and the addition of the observer to this thread
Always reproduce a bug before diagnosing it, and test the fix for cause rather than effect
Skills reach agents only by preload, and the dispatch tool goes to Leads only
Withdraw the report skill and put the answer-format standard in every agent body
Keep the code-reviewer agent, adopt receiving-code-review, drop requesting-code-review
Keep release-engineer broad; the real problem is per-duty procedure loading
The zero-compliance measurement was an instrumentation artifact; re-ground the channel thesis on documentation
The report artifact is outside repo scope, so its codename and CDN findings are ratified, not defects
Read the capability marker from the subagent's own output; scanning the parent transcript over-counts 52x

out_of_scope: Mutating any agent, rule, hook or skill file until the target architecture at c3 is approved. This is what makes the observer bug filed rather than fixed.
Restoring the bash gate's ask verdict so that destructive-operation confirmation becomes enforceable - that is a decision about the gate, not about agents, and it is filed in report section 14.

Cutting the standing instruction load for volume alone - round 4 reframed the question as re-scoping with path globs rather than cutting, and the false-claim fix and dead-reference deletions come first on correctness grounds.
Converting the report's nine Mermaid diagrams to inline SVG, and redacting the codename it carries - both ruled out of scope by the user and ratified as the validator's known baseline.
